title: Hamlet block-town render lab — reference notes
scope: A code-drawn, side-on/cutaway town study. The goal is the hierarchy and legibility of Kairosoft-like management scenes, not a reproduction of Kairosoft assets, UI, characters, names, or layouts.

questions.question: What camera makes floors and the street readable at one glance?
questions.answer: Use an orthographic side elevation with a shallow 6–10px downward reveal only in roofs and awnings. Treat the street as the bottom fifth of the frame; stack two 72px interior bays above it. This keeps the cutaway logic instantly readable and avoids the competing diagonals of an isometric map.

questions.question: What is the smallest useful sprite system?
questions.answer: Build on an 2px detail unit. A citizen is 16×24px, a door is 16×30px, a window is 20×20px, a shop bay is 72×56px, and a floor is 72px high including its slab. At that scale a person remains an intentional moving mark, while each room can still carry one unmistakable prop.

questions.question: How should road, citizens and buildings separate?
questions.answer: Give the road the darkest neutral and make it a clean horizontal band; set citizens in saturated, light-value tops; reserve the building outline for one dark ink. Put only 2–5 citizens on a screen-width scene and align their feet to a single pavement baseline.

questions.question: How dense should the detail be?
questions.answer: Use a three-speed rhythm: large masses every 72px (shop bays), medium anchors every 24–36px (windows, doors, trees), and tiny one-off accents every 48–96px (pot, lamp, parcel, cloud). Leave some bays calm so the eye can find movement.

questions.question: What does minimal signage mean here?
questions.answer: Every building earns one symbol-like sign, 14–24px wide, plus an optional 3–5 character wordmark outside the simulation view. The render itself should use motifs—book, cup, sun, envelope—not rows of tiny text.

sources.title: Mega Mall Story — App Store
observations: The listing describes a tower of shops, stairs, elevators and a heliport, confirming the core readable-unit idea: each floor is a distinct, shallow compartment with a single function.
The public screenshots are a useful reference for hierarchy in a management view: repeated floor bands, small character marks, and a few high-chroma functional anchors make a crowded scene scannable.
The reference informs construction rules only. No screenshot, sprite, UI framing, text, or game asset is copied into the local board.

sources.title: Mega Mall Story 2 — Google Play
observations: The listing explicitly presents a bigger, higher mall and different arrival modes, reinforcing that traffic and vertical circulation need to read as a few bold route marks rather than a field of micro-detail.
The official promotional frame makes each room legible by silhouette and color grouping before any label can be read; this is the right test for a phone-sized Hamlet town.

sources.title: Kairo Park — Kairosoft developer website
observations: Use it as provenance for the cited genre reference. The board retains an original, muted Hamlet palette and a side-on construction rather than borrowing the brand's presentation.

sources.title: Bean Town Mockup — local historical reference
sources.type: local reference, not a public source
observations: It establishes Hamlet's prior direction: a small town that grows gently, buildings as focused modules, a recurring little inhabitant, and no punishment for absence.

It uses a top-down/isometric block stand-in. This lab deliberately tests the requested side-on/cutaway alternative and should be evaluated as an art-direction study, not an implemented product decision.

construction_rules: Lock the camera to a straight-on orthographic elevation; use no vanishing-point perspective and no more than a 10px roof/awning top reveal.

Use two-unit detail increments with shallow shaded returns. The finished study uses 218-unit building parcels and 150-unit floor steps; residents are about 30 units tall. Avoid universal heavy outlines.
Separate the scene into five stable value bands: pale sky, building paper, medium-color facades, dark road, then dark ink outlines. A grayscale screenshot should still show those bands.
Make one building read as one verb: a book shelf, a kettle, a letter slot, a studio lamp. Put one primary prop in the room's upper half and keep the doorway clear.
Use a single continuous pavement baseline. Citizens touch it exactly; doors, planters and bus stops can interrupt it, but never float above it.
Allocate saturation as a navigation system: neutral architecture, one color family per place, and bright warm yellow only for active lights, parcels or a selected detail.
Repeat the structural cadence, not identical decoration: slabs align; roof pitches, window arrangements and accent colors alternate 1-2-1 across the street.
Limit in-render text to one short landmark wordmark per 3–4 buildings. Communicate most functions with a 2–3-color icon sign; keep complete labels in surrounding UI or accessible text.
pitfalls: Too many equal-weight windows, plants and signs flatten the scene. Preserve a quiet bay after every two busy bays.
A road that is too light loses pedestrian contrast; a road that is too tall makes the town feel like a traffic game. Keep it about 18–22% of scene height.
Generic pixel-noise dithering reads as texture, not care. Use small marks only when they explain material, use or change of state.
Tiny rendered copy becomes illegible at phone scale and makes localization painful. Keep labels semantic and external whenever possible.
Copying Kairosoft's interface chrome, exact palette, character designs, or recognizable room layouts would turn inspiration into imitation. Keep this study original in composition, palette and marks.
If every citizen has a different saturated outfit, they become confetti. Use two or three outfit colors and one movement cue at a time.
Hard black outlines on every interior object create visual static. Reserve the dark 4px outline for architecture and primary props; use color edges for secondary things.

handoff.recommended_start: The final study develops five parcels with fifteen furnished rooms from the initial three-building slice: post/letters, a reading room, and a warm evening cafe. Verify at 390px wide before adding a second floor or a fourth building.
handoff.do_not_import: Do not use source screenshots, extracted sprites, game names, logos, in-game UI or copied layout geometry in the product render.
